questions.q: What does the lesson say is more convincing than a slide deck when presenting this capstone?
options: A real, working prompt library, walked through live — including a live automated test run
A verbal description of what the prompt library would contain
A single screenshot of the folder structure
Reciting the course outline from memory
questions.explain: The lesson's core advice is that a real, running project — including running the automated test live and reporting the actual pass rate — is far more convincing than describing one.

questions.q: According to the suggested interview answer, why cap history and retrieval separately instead of using one combined budget number?
options: Because combined budgets are not supported by any model API
Because history and retrieval always cost the exact same number of tokens
So that neither history nor retrieval alone can silently consume the entire remaining context window
Because separate caps make the system prompt unnecessary
questions.explain: This callback to Lesson 13 explains that separate caps on each variable component prevent either one from growing unchecked and crowding out the rest of the budget.

questions.q: What does CHANGELOG.md demonstrate when presenting the capstone, according to this lesson?
options: Only the current date of the presentation
The real version history, including the documented A/B comparison winner and reason, and the specific regression the baseline caught
A list of unrelated future feature ideas
The original course outline
questions.explain: The lesson identifies CHANGELOG.md as the artifact that proves the A/B testing (Lesson 20) and regression testing (Lesson 21) work actually happened, with real documented results.

questions.q: What does the lesson say actually transfers from this course to future work, regardless of which model or provider is used?
options: The exact token limits of one specific model
Nothing; every new model requires starting over from scratch
Only the specific wording of the example system prompts used in this course
The discipline — budgets, ordering, eval sets, evidence-based iteration — not any one model's specific syntax
questions.explain: The lesson's closing point is that the engineering discipline (budgeting, ordering, testing, evidence over feeling) transfers across models and providers, while specific syntax and limits do not.

questions.q: Which course does this lesson name as coming next in the AI Engineer path?
options: RAG & Vector Databases
AI Agents
Docker and Deployment for AI Applications
Generative AI & LLMs
questions.explain: The lesson names RAG & Vector Databases as the next course, which builds the retrieval pipeline that feeds the context this course taught students to budget, order, and test.
